title.narrative: Women Advancing Inclusive, Participatory and Accountable Governance in the Bangsamoro (WAIPAGB) Project

description.narrative: The project seeks to strengthen the influence of women leaders and organizations in the Bangsamoro by enabling their active participation in governance and promoting accountability to the needs of women and the broader community. Through capacity-building activities such as participatory governance training, policy engagement, collaboration with established federations and municipal and regional duty bearers, and partnership to support literacy, women leaders will be equipped to meaningfully engage in local and regional decision-making. Simultaneously, women's organizations will lead efforts to assess and strengthen women’s desks and protection mechanisms through profiling and documentation, capacity building, partnerships with LGUs, and community dialogues on gender-based violence. To ensure sustainability and systemic support, the project will engage male leaders, traditional and religious leaders, and local government officials in dialogues and orientations to foster their advocacy for women’s participation in governance and political decision making. CRS will use the peaceful masculinities curriculum to inform engagement with male leaders to contribute towards gender-equitable masculine identity. Alongside with these efforts, success stories and a culminating learning event will collectively build a more inclusive and gender-responsive governance environment, empowering women and their organizations to shape policies, services, and accountability mechanisms in the BARMM.
